newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France Industries takes space in new Sogaris facility.
newsitem.headline: Air France Industries takes space in new Sogaris facility.

text.p: French freight installations operator, Sogaris, said Air France Industries, the aircraft maintenance division of the Air France group, will occupy 5,400 sq m of warehousing in the extension to its Centre Logistique de Fret Aerien (CLFA) at Paris-Charles de Gaulle airport.

The two building extension is due open on May 2. Costing 60 million francs, it will provide an extra 10,000 sq.m of warehousing and 2,200 sq m of office space boosting overall capacity at the site to 28,000 sq m of warehousing and 7,000 sq m of offices, a Sogaris official said.

KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV subsidiary, Cargo Service Centre (CSC) has dedicated facilities in the extension while Federal Express Corp is currently negotiating additional facilities at the CLFA, the official added.
The U.S. express operator already occupies 1,200 sq m of warehousing at the site, dedicated to aircraft maintenance.

"The extension is effectively fully-let and we will be spending the next few days finalising agreements with other tenants some of whom are new arrivals to the site while others are extending their existing facilities. We are now considering third-phase development of a 6,300 sq m building for use during 1998 and have already been contacted by potential tenants."
A longer-term objective is for the CLFA complex to be extended to cover 62,000 sq m, wholly-dedicated to airfreight activities, he added
Sogaris is 80 percent-owned by Paris area public authorities with the remaining 20 percent owned by private investors. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
